text:
Senator Rand Paul addresses COVID-19 investigation findings and food stamp amendment
K. E. Ibarra
Senator Rand Paul, chair of the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs, made several statements on July 22, 2026, regarding COVID-19 investigations and nutrition policy in federal assistance programs.
In a post published at 16:22 UTC, Paul credited Secretary Kennedy for assisting with efforts to uncover documents related to the handling of the COVID-19 pandemic. He stated, "Exposing the COVID cover-up would not have been made possible without @SecKennedy. Thanks to his help and cooperation in uncovering documents, we learned Biden's FBI stopped Border Patrol from investigating Peter Dazak, a key scientist in the gain-of-function research in Wuhan."
At 16:30 UTC on the same day, Paul shared a live event link with his followers: "LIVE NOW: https://t.co/VFBnr61oLF".
Later that afternoon at 17:59 UTC, he commented on legislative proceedings related to food stamp usage during a HELP markup session. Paul wrote, "Today in the HELP markup, I offered an amendment to stop food stamps from buying junk like Twinkies and Ding-Dongs. Same dollars, just no diabetes-causing garbage. Sixteen senators tabled it because kids might feel embarrassed without candy."
Paul’s public service extends beyond legislative work. According to his official website, he performs pro-bono eye surgeries for patients both in Kentucky and internationally (https://www.paul.senate.gov/), holds a medical degree from Duke University School of Medicine, and founded the Southern Kentucky Lions Eye Clinic. In addition to chairing the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs, he also assists Kentucky residents with issues involving federal agencies.
